collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Two parents' babies will only sleep to each other's lullabies: swap songs, or teach each other.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) live next door to each other, and both have babies who will not sleep. Last night (subject) noticed (subject.his/her) baby went quiet the moment (friend) started singing next door, and (friend)'s baby went quiet when (subject) sang. Both of them are exhausted. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Every night at sunset, (subject) and (friend) swap huts and sing each other's babies to sleep. It works perfectly. It is also, the neighbors point out, very strange. Neither parent cares. They are finally sleeping.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: They teach each other their lullabies. (subject)'s is about a fish who could not find the moon; (friend)'s is about a turtle who was very, very sleepy. The babies sleep. Soon half the parents in the village are singing about sleepy turtles.
